text:
ConocoPhillips rose modestly today as oil markets steadied after a sharp selloff earlier in the week. The stock had dropped nearly 3% by November 23rd following the collapse of climate negotiations at COP31, which raised fears of continued regulatory pressure on fossil fuel companies; today's gain reflects a partial recovery as crude prices stabilized around $82 per barrel domestically. The stock remains down about 2% over the two-week stretch, suggesting investors are still digesting longer-term concerns about the energy transition.

The bounce is also consistent with Wall Street's continued support for dividend-paying energy stocks like this one, which analysts have highlighted as attractive for income-focused investors despite near-term policy headwinds. Geopolitical developments—including Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries and speculation about restructuring of Russian oil assets—underscore ongoing supply-chain complexity but haven't significantly reset the broader crude price picture.
